scope.date_basis: Launch calendar date at Starbase, Texas.
excludes: Prototype hops and high-altitude SN tests

interpretation.observed: Publicly reported behavior; not an independent telemetry reconstruction.
interpretation.reported_cause: Source attribution retains provisional language. Null means no cause established by the selected sources.
interpretation.event_classification: Technical event classification is separate from whether FAA required a mishap investigation.
interpretation.planned_test_events: Intentional stress, disposition and destructive demonstrations are not automatic evidence of an unexpected failure.
interpretation.simulation_mapping: A candidate abstraction for the local simulator. It does not assert that SpaceX's physical cause or complete flight has been reproduced.
interpretation.probabilities: Scenario weights, timing and severity are test-design controls, not estimated Starship failure probabilities.
interpretation.empty_incidents: No unexpected anomaly verified in the selected official narrative; not proof that every subsystem was fault-free.

unsupported_physics: Propellant leaks, slosh and fluid-system pressure
limits: Engine, RCS and mechanism state changes represent bounded consequences only.
The catalog does not validate exact Starship mass, engine performance, aerodynamics or orbital dynamics.
Historical flight-control-team decisions are not evidence of LLM or MissionOS control.
Proposal, authorization, constraint checking, execution and verified outcome remain distinct.

historical_mapping_status.flap_jam: No verified primary mapping in this catalog. Synthetic scenario only; excluded from historically sourced defaults.

flights.summary: Control loss, delayed destruction and pad damage.

incidents.observed: Vehicle control was lost.
incidents.reported_cause: Propellant leakage, fire and lost engine communications.

simulation_mapping.note: Engine unavailability is a consequence proxy; fire and common-mode communications are unsupported.

limitations: Do not recast the separately planned electric thrust-vector-control upgrade as proof of a TVC failure.

incidents.observed: Flight-termination response was delayed.
Launch-pad foundation damaged.
limitations: Pad fracture and debris propagation are unsupported; this does not justify an in-flight tower-health injection.

incidents.observed: Booster lost during boostback.

simulation_mapping.note: Use unavailable engines only; feed-system physics are unsupported.

incidents.observed: Ship lost during ascent.
incidents.reported_cause: Leak and fire during oxidizer venting.

simulation_mapping.note: Represent thrust loss only; leakage, fire and flight termination are unsupported.

planned_test_events.event: Oxidizer venting was intentional; vehicle loss was not.

flights.summary: Booster thrust shortfall; ship attitude loss.

incidents.observed: Booster recovery thrust was insufficient.

simulation_mapping.note: Unavailable engines are a consequence proxy; filter physics are unsupported.

incidents.observed: Ship lost roll control.

simulation_mapping.note: Represent lost attitude-control authority; no valve or fluid-system reconstruction.

limitations: The planned in-space relight was skipped for attitude conditions, not attempted and failed.

flights.summary: Controlled reentry and both soft splashdowns reported.
flights.note: The inspected official postflight narrative does not establish the often-reported individual flap/heatshield damage or engine-out details. Those claims are excluded pending a verified primary passage.

regulatory_notes.note: Preflight test-induced-damage exceptions do not establish that a particular failure occurred.

flights.summary: First booster catch and planned ship splashdown.
flights.note: No unexpected anomaly verified in the selected official narrative; retain as an outcome/control entry.

flights.summary: Tower check prevented catch; booster diverted and soft-splashed.

incidents.observed: A critical tower-hardware health check stopped the catch attempt; the booster executed the preplanned ocean divert.
incidents.reported_cause: Tower health-check failure; specific component cause not established here.

simulation_mapping.note: Represent unavailable recovery infrastructure and the catch/divert decision.

limitations: Do not infer antenna, sensor or communication hardware damage without an additional primary source.

planned_test_events.event: Intentional thermal-protection and high-angle-of-attack tests are separate from the catch abort.

incidents.observed: Ship lost during ascent.

simulation_mapping.note: Thrust loss is a consequence proxy; vibration, leakage, combustion and breakup are unsupported.

limitations: Keep this mechanism distinct from Flight 8.

incidents.observed: One boostback engine startup aborted; it later restarted.

simulation_mapping.note: Temporary restart availability loss; ignition physics are unsupported.

regulatory_notes.note: Investigation closed March 28, 2025; FAA announced closure March 31.

flights.summary: Ship lost; booster caught with relight shortfalls.

incidents.observed: Ship lost during ascent.
incidents.reported_cause: Probable: Raptor hardware failure caused propellant mixing and ignition.

simulation_mapping.note: Represent thrust loss only; physical hardware failure and combustion are unsupported.

incidents.observed: Boostback lit 11/13 engines; landing lit 12/13.
incidents.reported_cause: Most probable: local igniter thermal conditions.

simulation_mapping.note: Represent restart availability only; igniter thermal physics are unsupported.

flights.summary: Upper stage lost after pressure and attitude anomalies; booster lost during its landing burn.

incidents.observed: Twelve of thirteen landing engines relit; an aft energetic event preceded telemetry loss.
incidents.reported_cause: Most probable: increased descent loads exceeded fuel-transfer-tube capability, allowing propellant mixing and ignition.

simulation_mapping.note: Reduced landing thrust is only a consequence proxy; structural failure and combustion are unsupported.

limitations: The higher-angle-of-attack experiment was intentional; the precise failure chain is reported as most probable.

incidents.observed: Fuel-tank pressure fell while nosecone pressure rose. Attitude error and door loads prevented payload deployment; passivation skipped the relight. Entry telemetry was lost.
incidents.reported_cause: Most probable: failure of the main fuel-tank pressurization diffuser.

simulation_mapping.note: Represent degraded attitude authority only; no leak-pressure dynamics.
Represent unavailable deployment only; not the historical door-pressure mechanism.

limitations: RCS was used to reduce the error; this source does not identify an RCS hardware failure.

planned_test_events.event: Higher-angle-of-attack booster descent and ocean splashdown target.

regulatory_notes.note: FAA investigated the upper-stage loss; booster loss fell within an approved test-induced-damage exception. Investigation closed August 15, 2025.

flights.summary: SpaceX reported all major objectives achieved, including payload demonstration, in-space relight and both ocean splashdowns.
flights.note: No unexpected anomaly is established by the selected official postflight narrative; this is not a claim that every subsystem was fault-free.

planned_test_events.event: A center engine was deliberately disabled during booster landing; a middle-ring engine provided backup.
Heatshield and structure were intentionally stressed; ship soft splashdown was planned.

flights.summary: All major objectives achieved; both vehicles completed planned ocean splashdowns.

incidents.observed: One of thirteen planned boostback engines did not relight; all thirteen later ignited for landing.

simulation_mapping.note: Temporary engine unavailability with later recovery; engine startup physics are unsupported.

limitations: The public narrative does not identify the underlying mechanical cause.

planned_test_events.event: Booster landing-profile experiment and intentional upper-stage heatshield stress and banking maneuver.

flights.summary: Upper stage reached its planned trajectory despite engine loss and splashed down; booster recovery failed.

incidents.observed: One ascent engine stopped. Incomplete boostback ignition led to early cutoff; landing ignition was attempted before a hard splashdown.
incidents.reported_cause: FAA accepted heat effects on propulsion components during ascent and erroneous engine-alarm settings as two most-probable causes of booster loss.

simulation_mapping.note: Represent ascent engine unavailability only, not the physical failure mechanism.
Represent unavailable engines and thrust consequences; thermal and alarm-system mechanisms are unsupported.

limitations: Do not assign each individual engine event to one specific cause without further evidence.

incidents.observed: One vacuum engine was lost during ascent; engine-out operation still achieved the planned trajectory. Landing used two engines.

simulation_mapping.note: Reduced available thrust is a proxy; the local simulator is not a calibrated V3 vehicle model.

limitations: The selected official postflight narrative does not explain the vacuum-engine failure or establish why landing used two engines.

planned_test_events.event: Suborbital payload demonstration, rear-flap structural stress, banking maneuver and ocean splashdown were planned tests.

regulatory_notes.note: FAA classified booster return as a mishap on May 27; investigation closed July 13, 2026.

flights.summary: Booster hard-splashed after incomplete recovery burns; ship deployed its test payload and splashed down intact.

incidents.observed: Boostback ended early; only a subset of landing engines relit before a hard splashdown.
incidents.reported_cause: SpaceX's Flight 14 preflight account described signs of ice clogging in three center engines late in Flight 13 boostback.

simulation_mapping.note: Represent engine availability loss only; ice formation, filtration and feed-system physics are unsupported.

limitations: Cause detail comes from a search-indexed preflight edition of the official Flight 14 page; its current canonical narrative has been replaced by the postflight report.
Signs of ice clogging are not an independently verified complete root-cause chain.

planned_test_events.event: Twenty satellites were deployed suborbitally for a test and expected to demise on reentry; this was not failure to place an operational constellation in orbit.

flights.summary: First orbital flight; deployed 26 satellites and returned to an alternate, pre-coordinated Pacific zone.

incidents.observed: One ascent engine stopped; 31 of 33 planned boostback engines and 11 of 13 landing engines relit.

simulation_mapping.note: Represent ascent engine unavailability only, not the physical failure mechanism.
Represent reduced engine availability only; no exact multi-engine V3 reconstruction.

limitations: The published narrative does not establish root causes.

incidents.observed: A vacuum engine stopped early. Longer operation of the other five engines compensated. Controllers shortened orbital duration and completed alternate-zone deorbit and splashdown.

simulation_mapping.note: Use reduced thrust as a mission-replanning stimulus, not as a validated replay of this flight.

limitations: No claim about exact vehicle masses, engine parameters or reproduced orbital dynamics.
Health assessment, permission to proceed, execution and observed splashdown are separate facts.

planned_test_events.event: Booster oxidizer depletion experiment and flight-termination-system demonstration after landing-burn shutdown were deliberate.

sources.edition_note: Search-indexed Flight 14 preflight text; current canonical page is the postflight report.
